newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Grameen Phone links Bangladesh villagers to PM.
newsitem.headline: Grameen Phone links Bangladesh villagers to PM.

text.p: Laili Begum of Patira village near Dhaka made a brave leap into a high-tech world of communications on Wednesday when she spoke to Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on a mobile phone from her home.
It was made possible by the launch of Bangladesh's first rural telecom network by Grameen Phone, a joint venture between three overseas telephone companies and a local company.
The venture also spelled the end of a seven-year monopoly in cellular mobile business by City Cell, another local private company and a unit of Pacific Bangladesh Telecom Ltd.
City Cell had been the lone operator in the field since 1989 but services were restricted to Dhaka. The company has said, however, it now plans to extend its service to the port city of Chittagong.
"How are you Madam? Please come to my village some time. May Allah bless you and your children," Begum, who had never used a telephone before, told the prime minister.
Hasina wished her well and congratulated her on becoming a proud owner of a mobile phone.
Patira villagers celebrated the occasion by dancing and singing. "We are in a new world," said Begum, flanked by other women.
Begum subscribed to the phone for 18,100 taka ($420), which she borrowed from the Grameen Bank, the world famous micro credit bank.
Begum, a cattle breeder, said she would let other villagers use the phone on payment. She has yet to fix call charges.
Company officials said the Grameen Phone had for the first time extended telephone services to rural areas.

"Never before did anyone think of giving a telephone to the rural people. We plan to reach at least 50 percent of the country's 80,000 villages in the next four years," Shahed Latif, Managing Director of Grameen Telecom, told Reuters in Patira.
Grameen Telecom, a subsidiary of the Grameen Bank, owns 35 percent of the Grameen Phone.
Telenor, a state-run Norwegian telephone company, has a 51 percent stake, Japan's Marubeni Corp 9.5 percent and U.S.-based Gonofone 3.5 percent.
Hasina also spoke on Wednesday to her Norwegian counterpart, Torbjorn Jagland, over the telephone to mark the Grameen Phone launch.
Grameen Phone has so far invested 800 million taka ($19 million) in the project and said it is now ready to provide 6,500 connections in Dhaka city and nearby villages.
Company officials said investment would reach up to three billion taka ($70 million) by the year 2,000 when they expect to cover the whole of Bangladesh.
The officials said the company was holding discussions with the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the International Finance Corporation (IFC) regarding credit.
Telecommunication Ministry officials said two more companies -- Seba Telecom and TM International -- had been given permission to operate cellular mobile telephones in the country.
